name: Diarrhoea and Vomiting
source_guidance: Adapted from WHO guidance on assessing dehydration and treating diarrhoea with oral rehydration salts (ORS), WHO cholera guidance, and NHS 111 guidance on diarrhoea and vomiting.

questions.text: Is the person very drowsy, confused, or unconscious?
Is the person unable to drink, or vomiting everything so no fluid stays down?
Is there vomiting of blood or dark material like coffee grounds, or black stool with dizziness or fainting?
Is there a large amount of watery diarrhoea that looks like rice water, with very little urine or sunken eyes?
Is there blood in the stool?
Has the person passed little or no urine in the last 8 hours, or are they very thirsty with a dry mouth?
Is the person pregnant, over 65, or living with diabetes, kidney disease, or HIV?
Has the diarrhoea lasted more than 14 days?

emergency: Call 112 now, or get to the nearest hospital emergency department immediately.
Give oral rehydration salts (ORS) in small, frequent sips on the way if the person can swallow.
Severe watery diarrhoea can be cholera. Wash hands with soap and water after any contact.
Do not drive yourself. Ask someone to take you, or wait for the ambulance.
urgent: Go to a clinic or hospital today.
Start oral rehydration salts (ORS) now: give a cup after each loose stool, in small sips if vomiting.
Call 112 if the person becomes drowsy or cannot keep any fluid down.
routine: Book a clinic appointment within the next few days for tests.
Keep drinking ORS or clean fluids and keep eating normal food.
Call back at once if symptoms get worse or new symptoms appear.
self_care: Drink oral rehydration salts (ORS) or clean fluids after each loose stool.
Keep eating light, normal food in small amounts.
Wash hands with soap and water after using the toilet and before preparing food.
Drink only safe water: boiled, treated, or sealed.
Call back at once if symptoms get worse or new symptoms appear.
